task_3.title: Disable CMake package registry exports by default
task_3.description: Conan 2.27.0 changes CMakeToolchain so generated CMake toolchains no longer export packages into the user's CMake package registry by default. This restores the earlier Conan behavior, reduces unintended global registry side effects, and ensures the default is honored even when the project declares an older CMake minimum version.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that projects using Conan's CMakeToolchain do not write package entries into the CMake user package registry by default, while still allowing consumers to keep an explicit registry export configuration if they already set one.

expectation.grounded: CMakeToolchain should generate a toolchain that disables CMake package registry exports by default. The generated behavior should activate CMake policy CMP0090 so export(PACKAGE) follows CMAKE_EXPORT_PACKAGE_REGISTRY even when the project uses a CMake minimum version below 3.15. When CMAKE_EXPORT_PACKAGE_REGISTRY is not already defined, it should default to disabled; release-note semantics also require package-registry export controls to remain off by default unless the consumer explicitly defines otherwise.
expectation.conceptual: Using Conan's CMake integration should no longer pollute the developer's global CMake package registry unless the project intentionally opts in. The default should be safe, predictable, and effective across supported CMake policy configurations, while respecting any explicit registry export choice already made by the consuming project.

constraints.grounded: Do not override an explicitly defined CMAKE_EXPORT_PACKAGE_REGISTRY value. The change should affect default toolchain behavior only and should not require consumers to modify their project configuration to preserve an intentional opt-in. The policy adjustment must only ensure correct interpretation of the registry export setting.
constraints.conceptual: Keep explicit user configuration authoritative, and only change the default behavior for projects that did not already choose a package-registry export setting. Prevent new unintended global side effects without removing the ability to opt in deliberately.

behavior: Generated CMake toolchains now set policy CMP0090 to ensure export(PACKAGE) obeys the package registry export setting.
If the consuming project has not defined CMAKE_EXPORT_PACKAGE_REGISTRY, the generated toolchain disables it by default.
The default behavior prevents package exports from being written to the user's CMake package registry unless the project explicitly enables that behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan generates a CMake toolchain for a project that does not define CMAKE_EXPORT_PACKAGE_REGISTRY, package registry export should be disabled by default.
When a project using the generated toolchain performs CMake package export operations, it should not create entries in the user's CMake package registry unless the project explicitly opted in.
When the consuming project already defines CMAKE_EXPORT_PACKAGE_REGISTRY, Conan should preserve that explicit setting instead of replacing it with the default.
When the project declares a CMake minimum version lower than 3.15, the generated toolchain should still make the package registry export setting effective for export(PACKAGE).

task_1.title: Support grouped negated profile tool-requires patterns
task_1.description: Upgrading to 2.27.0 adds support for grouped negated OR patterns in profile [tool_requires] entries, so one rule can exclude multiple package-reference patterns while still applying the tool requirement everywhere else. This makes profile-based tool requirement overrides more expressive and helps avoid build-context dependency cycles without changing recipe declarations.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that profile [tool_requires] rules can exclude multiple reference patterns with a single negated OR expression so tool requirements can be applied to all other packages while avoiding build-context dependency cycles.

expectation.grounded: Profile [tool_requires] matching must accept grouped negated patterns such as !(pattern1|pattern2|...) when deciding whether a tool requirement override applies to a package reference. The grouped rule must match only when the current reference matches none of the pipe-separated branches under the existing reference-matching semantics, and matching tool requirements must then be applied through the normal profile override flow in the active host or build context. A grouped negated expression without its closing parenthesis must be rejected rather than silently treated as a normal pattern.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare one profile tool-requirement rule that applies everywhere except a specified set of package patterns. Packages that match any excluded branch should not receive that tool requirement from the profile, while all other packages should. Invalid grouped exclusion syntax should fail clearly instead of producing ambiguous behavior.

constraints.grounded: Existing non-grouped [tool_requires] pattern matching must continue to behave the same way. Grouped negated OR support must only change rule-selection semantics for profile tool requirement overrides, preserve consumer-aware reference matching, and leave existing self-loop avoidance for build requirements intact.
constraints.conceptual: The new exclusion syntax should extend current matching behavior without changing unrelated profile rules or introducing new self-dependency behavior. Existing ordinary patterns and normal tool-requirement resolution should continue to work as before.

behavior: A profile [tool_requires] pattern that uses a negation operator followed by parentheses is interpreted as a grouped OR exclusion over its pipe-separated branches.
The grouped rule matches a package reference only if none of the grouped branches match that reference under the same matching logic used for ordinary profile patterns.
When the grouped negated rule matches, its declared tool requirements are applied through the existing profile override mechanism for the relevant dependency context.
Malformed grouped negated expressions that do not close the parenthesized branch list cause evaluation to fail instead of being accepted as valid grouped rules.
acceptance_criteria: When a profile [tool_requires] entry uses !(a|b|c):tool/version, a package reference matching a, b, or c should not receive that tool requirement from the profile rule.
When a package reference matches none of the grouped exclusion branches, it should receive the specified tool requirement exactly as it would for any other matching profile tool-requires rule.

When grouped negation is used in a build-profile tool requirement to avoid a cycle for selected package references, the excluded references should not get the extra tool requirement while non-excluded references still can.
When a grouped negated pattern is malformed because the closing parenthesis is missing, processing should fail instead of treating the entry as a valid grouped exclusion rule.

task_2.title: Add CVSS version details to conan audit results
task_2.description: Upgrade `conan audit` so vulnerability results expose richer CVSS scoring information. In addition to the existing preferred score, audit output should surface version-specific CVSS v3 and v4 base scores when the provider returns them, while remaining compatible with older responses that only include the preferred score.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan audit` shows richer CVSS information in vulnerability results so users can see the preferred score and any available CVSS version-specific scores without breaking existing audit output for older vulnerability data.

expectation.grounded: `conan audit` should retrieve `cvss.preferredBaseScore` together with optional `cvss.v3.baseScore` and `cvss.v4.baseScore` from the audit provider. In text output, each vulnerability should display severity with the preferred score inline when present, and should print separate `CVSS v3` and `CVSS v4` lines only when those base scores are available and positive. In HTML output, the severity badge should include the preferred score when present, and the rendered vulnerability details should include separate CVSS v3 and v4 values when available.
expectation.conceptual: Audit results should show more complete CVSS scoring details. Users should see the main score directly with the vulnerability severity, plus version-specific CVSS v3 and v4 scores when the provider knows them, across the supported audit result views.

constraints.grounded: Responses that only contain `preferredBaseScore` must continue to render successfully. `conan audit` must not require `cvss.v3` or `cvss.v4` to exist, and it should omit version-specific CVSS entries when the score is missing or non-positive. Existing vulnerability metadata such as severity, identifiers, descriptions, aliases, references, fix versions, and withdrawn state must remain available in the output.
constraints.conceptual: Older vulnerability records must still work, and extra CVSS details should appear only when real version-specific score data is available. The upgrade should extend audit output without removing existing vulnerability information.

behavior: `conan audit` requests CVSS version data in addition to the preferred base score.
Text-formatted audit results show the preferred score inline with the displayed severity when that score exists.
Text-formatted audit results add separate labeled entries for CVSS v3 and CVSS v4 only when those base scores are present and greater than zero.
HTML-formatted audit results include the preferred score inside the severity badge when available.
HTML-formatted audit results render CVSS v3 and CVSS v4 as separate visible details for each vulnerability when those scores are available.
If only the preferred score is provided, audit output continues to display the vulnerability without version-specific CVSS details.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan audit` receives a vulnerability with `preferredBaseScore` only, it should display the severity together with that preferred score and should not show CVSS v3 or CVSS v4 details.

When `conan audit` receives a vulnerability with `preferredBaseScore` and `cvss.v3.baseScore`, it should include the preferred score in the main vulnerability summary and should show a separate CVSS v3 entry.

When `conan audit` receives a vulnerability with `preferredBaseScore` and `cvss.v4.baseScore`, it should include the preferred score in the main vulnerability summary and should show a separate CVSS v4 entry.
When `conan audit` receives both `cvss.v3.baseScore` and `cvss.v4.baseScore`, it should show both version-specific scores in addition to the preferred score.
When version-specific CVSS scores are absent or non-positive, `conan audit` should suppress those version-specific entries rather than failing or showing placeholder values.
When users view audit results in either text or HTML form, the richer CVSS information should be presented consistently with the output style of that format.

task_6.title: Add transitive requirement visibility to HTML dependency graphs
task_6.description: The Conan 2.27.0 HTML graph output adds an interactive way to reveal transitive requirements in dependency visualizations. This keeps the default graph focused on direct relationships while letting users inspect indirect dependency propagation on demand.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the HTML dependency graph can show transitive requirements on demand so users can inspect indirect dependency relationships without cluttering the default view.

expectation.grounded: The HTML formatter used by `conan graph info --format=html` should expose a `Show transitive-requires` control. On initial load, direct dependency edges should remain visible as before and dependencies marked as non-direct should remain hidden. When the control is enabled, transitive requirement relationships should be rendered in the graph as visually distinct secondary edges, and the graph should redraw without disabling existing build-require, test-require, conflict, loop, or package-grouping behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users viewing the generated HTML dependency graph should be able to opt into seeing indirect dependencies. The graph should stay readable by default, then reveal transitive relationships in a clearly differentiated way when requested, while preserving the rest of the interactive graph behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not make transitive requirements visible by default. Existing direct dependency rendering and the current interactive filters for build requirements, test requirements, and package grouping must continue to work. When shown, transitive relationships must remain distinguishable from direct edges and must not suppress existing loop or conflict indicators already present in the graph.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the default HTML graph focused on the same primary relationships users already see today. Adding optional indirect links must not break or reinterpret existing graph controls, diagnostics, or direct dependency visibility.

behavior: The generated HTML graph includes a new `Show transitive-requires` toggle that is initially disabled.
While the toggle is disabled, dependency links classified as transitive or non-direct are not drawn in the graph.
When the toggle is enabled, transitive requirement links are added between the corresponding package nodes as visually secondary connections.
Changing the transitive-requirement toggle redraws the graph and coexists with the existing build-require, test-require, and package-grouping controls.
Existing loop visualization behavior continues to appear in the HTML graph while transitive requirement handling is applied.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency graph is exported to HTML and opened, it should present direct dependency relationships without showing transitive requirement links by default.

Given a graph that contains indirect dependencies, when the user enables `Show transitive-requires`, the HTML graph should reveal those indirect relationships as distinct secondary links while keeping the already visible direct links intact.
When the user disables `Show transitive-requires` after enabling it, the indirect relationship links should disappear again without removing the direct dependency links.
When the user changes the build-require, test-require, or package-grouping controls, the transitive requirement toggle should continue to function correctly after the graph redraws.
When loop indicators are present in the graph data, they should remain visible even when transitive requirement visibility is toggled.

task_5.title: Align PyEnv pip and uv output with Conan verbosity
task_5.description: Conan 2.27.0 updates PyEnv so that pip-based package installation and uv-based virtual environment creation follow the current Conan verbosity level. This makes routine output quieter at low verbosity, more detailed at high verbosity, and keeps default status-level behavior unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that PyEnv respects the active Conan verbosity level when invoking pip and uv so users get appropriately quiet or detailed command output without changing virtual-environment creation or package-install behavior.

expectation.grounded: The public PyEnv workflow in conan.tools.system should propagate ConanOutput verbosity to the underlying pip and uv commands used by PyEnv.install() and by uv-backed environment creation. Quiet, error, and warning levels should reduce routine pip and uv output; verbose, debug, and trace levels should increase it; and the normal status level should continue without an added verbosity override. Failures from PyEnv-managed installs must still surface as errors instead of being hidden by quieter output settings.
expectation.conceptual: When users choose a Conan verbosity level, PyEnv should make its Python package installation and virtual-environment setup output match that choice. Lower verbosity should suppress nonessential noise, higher verbosity should expose more command detail, and ordinary default usage should behave as before while still reporting failures clearly.

constraints.grounded: This change must not alter interpreter selection, selected packages, whether PyEnv uses pip or uv, environment creation success criteria, or package installation semantics. It should only affect how much output pip and uv emit, and it must preserve the default behavior when Conan runs at status-level verbosity.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should change output volume only. It must not change what PyEnv installs, how environments are created, or whether operations succeed or fail, and it must not make default logging noisier or quieter than before unless the user explicitly selects another verbosity level.

behavior: PyEnv.install() now adjusts pip's native verbosity according to the active Conan output level instead of always using pip's default output behavior.
When PyEnv bootstraps uv through pip, that pip invocation follows the same Conan-driven verbosity mapping as other PyEnv package installations.
When PyEnv creates a virtual environment through uv, the uv command now receives quiet or verbose output settings derived from the active Conan verbosity level.
At Conan status-level output, PyEnv does not add an explicit pip or uv verbosity override, preserving the previous default command output behavior.
Reducing verbosity should suppress routine pip and uv chatter, but failed package installation or environment setup must still be surfaced to the user as an error condition.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs a workflow that calls PyEnv.install() under quiet, error, or warning verbosity, pip should emit less routine output than it does at the default level while the installation behavior remains unchanged.
When a user runs a workflow that calls PyEnv.install() under verbose, debug, or trace verbosity, pip should emit more diagnostic detail than it does at the default level.
When PyEnv creates a virtual environment using uv, the uv command output should become quieter at low Conan verbosity and more detailed at high Conan verbosity.
When Conan runs at the normal status verbosity, PyEnv package installation and uv environment creation should keep the prior default output behavior rather than forcing extra quiet or verbose modes.
When a PyEnv-managed package install fails under reduced verbosity, the user should still receive a visible failure outcome rather than a silent or hidden error.

task_4.title: Remove legacy Conan 1.x alias requirement support
task_4.description: Conan 2.27.0 removes legacy Conan 1.x alias support from dependency resolution. Alias-based requirements that previously redirected to another recipe now fail by default, with only a temporary environment-variable compatibility override remaining for users who still need the old behavior during migration.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.27.0 no longer relies on legacy Conan 1.x alias requirements, because alias-based dependencies are removed and should fail by default unless an explicit temporary compatibility override is enabled.

expectation.grounded: During dependency graph resolution in Conan 2.27.0, if a requirement is an alias requirement, Conan should raise a ConanException by default instead of resolving the alias target. Legacy alias traversal should only remain available when the compatibility override CONAN_ALLOW_ALIAS is set to the exact value will_break_next.
expectation.conceptual: Alias recipes from Conan 1.x are no longer a supported dependency mechanism. Operations that encounter an alias should stop with an error by default rather than transparently redirecting to another package, while a temporary opt-in compatibility switch may still allow old alias-based graphs to resolve.

constraints.grounded: Requirements that are not aliases must continue to resolve normally. The default failure must be limited to alias requirements encountered while building the dependency graph, and the only compatibility bypass described by the change is the explicit CONAN_ALLOW_ALIAS=will_break_next override.
constraints.conceptual: Normal dependency resolution should remain unchanged for direct dependencies. Only legacy alias indirection should be blocked by default, and any short-term compatibility path should require an explicit user opt-in.

behavior: Alias requirements are rejected by default during dependency graph construction.
When an alias requirement is encountered without the compatibility override, Conan raises ConanException instead of following the aliased reference.
Setting CONAN_ALLOW_ALIAS to will_break_next temporarily restores the previous alias-resolution path for compatibility.
Alias rejection happens before legacy alias replacement logic can continue, so alias-based resolution no longer succeeds implicitly.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan operation builds a dependency graph containing an alias requirement and no compatibility override is set, it should fail with ConanException instead of resolving the aliased package.
When a dependency graph contains only non-alias requirements, it should resolve with the same behavior as before this change.
When CONAN_ALLOW_ALIAS=will_break_next is explicitly set and an alias requirement is encountered, Conan should allow the legacy alias flow to continue instead of failing immediately.
When an alias would previously have been resolved through existing alias-replacement behavior, Conan should still reject it by default unless the compatibility override is enabled.

task_7.title: Add support for Clang 22 compiler settings
task_7.description: The update adds user-facing support for Clang 22 by recognizing it as a valid compiler version in the library's default settings model. This allows consumers targeting the newest Clang release to use standard compiler settings without those configurations being rejected as unsupported.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can target Clang 22 through the standard compiler settings model and that configurations using `compiler=clang` with version `22` are accepted as supported.

expectation.grounded: The default settings schema must include `22` as a supported value for `compiler=clang` under `compiler.version`. Any profile, package configuration, or settings-driven workflow that uses `compiler.version=22` with the Clang compiler should be treated as valid by settings validation and should not fail solely because that version was previously unsupported.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare Clang 22 the same way they declare other supported Clang versions. The system should recognize that compiler version as valid and allow normal processing to continue instead of rejecting the configuration.

constraints.grounded: This change is additive to the supported Clang version list. Existing accepted Clang versions and other compiler-related settings dimensions must continue to behave as before, and no unrelated compiler families should be affected.
constraints.conceptual: Adding support for the new compiler release must not break existing compiler configurations or change behavior outside the intended Clang 22 support.

behavior: The built-in supported values for the Clang compiler version now include `22`.
When a user supplies `compiler=clang` together with `compiler.version=22`, the configuration is recognized as valid by default settings validation.
Workflows that previously failed only because Clang 22 was not an accepted compiler version should now proceed under the same validation rules applied to other supported Clang versions.
acceptance_criteria: When a user defines a configuration with `compiler=clang` and `compiler.version=22`, the library should accept that settings combination as supported.
When a profile or package configuration targets Clang 22, it should not raise an unsupported or invalid settings error solely because the compiler version is `22`.
When a user continues to target previously supported Clang versions, their configurations should remain accepted with no change in behavior.

task_9.title: Support resource compiler flags via Conan build configuration
task_9.description: Conan 2.27.0 adds a new `tools.build:rcflags` configuration so users can pass resource compiler flags through generated build toolchains and profiles instead of having those flags ignored or handled out of band.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan users can declare extra resource compiler flags through a dedicated `tools.build:rcflags` configuration and have those flags propagated consistently to supported generated toolchains and profiles.

expectation.grounded: Conan must recognize `tools.build:rcflags` as a list-valued built-in configuration for extra RC/resource-compiler flags. When this configuration is set, `CMakeToolchain`, `MSBuildToolchain`, `NMakeToolchain`, `AutotoolsToolchain`, `GnuToolchain`, `PremakeToolchain`, and `QbsProfile` must expose those flags through their normal public output channels for resource compilation, such as RC-related CMake initialization variables, MSBuild `ResourceCompile` options, `RCFLAGS` environment variables, Premake resource-file build options, and Qbs `cpp.rcFlags`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to define resource compiler flags once in Conan configuration and have generated build integrations carry those flags into resource compilation in the same way existing compile and link flag settings already work.

constraints.grounded: The new configuration must accept only list-form flag values, must not change the behavior of existing `tools.build:cflags`, `tools.build:cxxflags`, `tools.build:sharedlinkflags`, `tools.build:exelinkflags`, or `tools.build:defines`, and must not inject RC-specific settings when `tools.build:rcflags` is unset or empty. Toolchains that scope flags by build configuration must preserve that scoping for RC flags as well.
constraints.conceptual: The added RC flag support must be additive and non-breaking: existing flag handling should keep working as before, empty RC flag configuration should have no effect, and any per-configuration behavior already present in generated outputs should remain intact.

behavior: Conan provides a new `tools.build:rcflags` configuration entry for specifying extra resource compiler flags.

When `tools.build:rcflags` is configured, `CMakeToolchain` propagates those flags into its RC-related initialization output, including generic and configuration-specific RC flag initialization where applicable.
When `tools.build:rcflags` is configured, `MSBuildToolchain` adds those flags to the generated `ResourceCompile` options used for resource compilation.
When `tools.build:rcflags` is configured, `NMakeToolchain`, `AutotoolsToolchain`, and `GnuToolchain` export the flags through the `RCFLAGS` environment variable for downstream build tools.
When `tools.build:rcflags` is configured, `PremakeToolchain` applies those flags to resource compilation for `.rc` files rather than to unrelated compile or link settings.
When `tools.build:rcflags` is configured, `QbsProfile` maps the values into the generated Qbs resource-compiler flag property.
When `tools.build:rcflags` is not provided, generated outputs omit RC-specific additions and continue to behave as before.
acceptance_criteria: When a user sets `tools.build:rcflags` to a list of flags and generates a `CMakeToolchain`, the generated CMake toolchain output should include those flags in the RC initialization variables used by CMake.
When a user sets `tools.build:rcflags` and generates an `MSBuildToolchain`, resource compilation in the generated MSBuild configuration should receive those flags through `ResourceCompile` options.
When a user sets `tools.build:rcflags` and generates `NMakeToolchain`, `AutotoolsToolchain`, or `GnuToolchain`, the generated environment should expose the configured flags through `RCFLAGS`.
When a user sets `tools.build:rcflags` and generates a `PremakeToolchain`, the resulting configuration should apply those flags to `.rc` resource files.
When a user sets `tools.build:rcflags` and generates a `QbsProfile`, the resulting profile should expose the configured values as resource compiler flags for Qbs.
When `tools.build:rcflags` is omitted or empty, toolchain generation should not add RC-specific flags and existing compile, link, and define behavior should remain unchanged.

task_10.title: Add Apple OS 26.3 settings support
task_10.description: The update adds first-class support for Apple 26.3 operating system releases in the library's built-in settings model so consumers can target those platform versions without settings validation failures.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that projects targeting Apple OS 26.3 releases can declare those platform versions in library settings and profiles without being rejected as unsupported.

expectation.grounded: The library should treat `os.version=26.3` as a valid built-in setting value for `iOS`, `watchOS`, `tvOS`, `visionOS`, and `Macos`, consistent with the existing Apple version lists. Public behavior that consumes built-in settings, such as profile parsing and settings validation, should accept these values instead of failing due to an unknown `os.version` entry.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to target Apple 26.3 platform releases across the supported Apple operating systems using normal configuration flows, and the library should recognize those version identifiers as supported settings.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to recognizing `26.3` in the built-in `os.version` value sets for the supported Apple operating systems. Existing valid versions, platform names, SDK names, and SDK version behavior should remain unchanged, and no new support should be implied for other operating systems or unrelated setting dimensions.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should expand compatibility for the new Apple OS patch release without altering existing behavior for other platforms or changing unrelated configuration rules.

behavior: When the selected operating system is `iOS`, `watchOS`, `tvOS`, `visionOS`, or `Macos`, the library now recognizes `26.3` as an allowed `os.version` value.

Configurations, profiles, or recipes that declare one of those Apple operating systems with `os.version=26.3` should proceed through normal settings validation instead of being rejected as unsupported.
Support is additive: previously accepted Apple `os.version` values remain valid, and operating systems outside the updated Apple set are unaffected.
The update concerns operating system version recognition only and does not change the accepted SDK identifiers or SDK version lists.
acceptance_criteria: When a user configures `iOS` with `os.version` set to `26.3`, the library should accept the setting as valid.
When a user configures `watchOS` with `os.version` set to `26.3`, the library should accept the setting as valid.
When a user configures `tvOS` with `os.version` set to `26.3`, the library should accept the setting as valid.
When a user configures `visionOS` with `os.version` set to `26.3`, the library should accept the setting as valid.
When a user configures `Macos` with `os.version` set to `26.3`, the library should accept the setting as valid.
When users continue to use previously supported Apple OS version values, behavior should remain unchanged.
When users configure SDK names or SDK versions, the accepted values should remain the same as before this update.

task_8.title: Visualize dependency loops in HTML graph output
task_8.description: Conan 2.27.0 enhances `conan graph info --format=html` so dependency cycles are represented in the generated graph, not just reported as an error. Loop errors now provide structured graph data that lets the HTML view highlight the relationship that closes the cycle with a distinct visual marker.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan graph info --format=html` visibly identifies dependency cycles in the rendered graph so users can immediately see which dependency closes the loop when graph resolution fails due to a cycle.

expectation.grounded: When `conan graph info --format=html` encounters a `GraphLoopError`, the graph error payload should serialize as error type `loop` and expose the involved `node`, `require`, and `ancestor` information needed by the formatter. The HTML graph renderer should detect that `loop` error and draw the dependency edge that closes the cycle as a distinct red curved arrow labeled as a loop. Existing handling for `conflict`, `provide_conflict`, and `missing` graph errors should remain intact.
expectation.conceptual: If the dependency graph contains a cycle, the HTML graph view should make the loop obvious by visually highlighting the relationship that creates the cycle, instead of leaving users to infer it from a generic failure.

constraints.grounded: The new visualization should apply only to loop errors and should not change the normal rendering of successful graphs or the separate handling of other graph error types. Loop detection must still be surfaced as an error condition even when HTML output is generated, and existing graph visibility filters should remain compatible with the rendered result.
constraints.conceptual: Regular graphs should continue to render normally, and non-loop failures should continue to be represented in their usual way. The loop marker should add clarity without changing the fact that a cyclic graph is invalid.

behavior: `GraphLoopError` now contributes structured `loop` error information to the graph data used by HTML formatting.
When the HTML formatter receives graph data whose error type is `loop`, it identifies the node-to-dependency relationship that closes the cycle.
The loop-closing relationship is rendered as a visually distinct red arrow with loop labeling so it stands out from ordinary dependency edges.
Loop-specific rendering is handled separately from existing conflict, provide-conflict, and missing-dependency visual states.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency graph contains a cycle and `conan graph info --format=html` is generated, the resulting HTML graph should visibly mark the dependency edge that closes the cycle with a red loop indicator.
When a loop is present, the highlighted relationship should connect the package that declares the problematic requirement to the package/reference that repeats in the ancestor chain.
When the graph does not contain a cycle, the HTML graph should not display the loop marker.

When the graph fails for conflict, provided-package conflict, or missing dependency reasons instead of a loop, the HTML output should continue using the existing non-loop error handling rather than the loop marker.

task_11.title: Support extra arguments for CMake.configure()
task_11.description: Conan 2.27.0 adds a new `tools.cmake:configure_args` configuration so consumers can pass additional command-line arguments to `CMake.configure()`, including cache definitions and flags such as `--fresh`, without changing recipe code. When the setting is not used, existing configure behavior remains unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan users can supply additional command-line arguments to the CMake configure step through configuration, so `CMake.configure()` can receive extra CMake variables and flags such as `--fresh` without altering existing recipe behavior.

expectation.grounded: Expose `tools.cmake:configure_args` as a built-in Conan configuration for `CMake.configure()`. When this configuration is set to a list of argument strings, `CMake.configure()` should append those arguments to the generated CMake configure command after the CMakeLists/source folder argument and before any automatically added log-level options. This must allow both CMake variable definitions and other supported configure-time flags.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to configure extra arguments for the CMake configure phase through Conan configuration, and those arguments should be forwarded as part of the configure invocation in the order supplied.

constraints.grounded: If `tools.cmake:configure_args` is unset, `CMake.configure()` should behave as before and add no extra configure arguments. The setting applies only to the configure invocation and must not change the behavior of other CMake actions. The configuration value is a list, and each entry should be propagated as its own command-line argument.
constraints.conceptual: Existing consumers should see no behavior change unless they opt into the new setting. Extra arguments should affect only the configure step and should pass through transparently rather than being reformatted or repurposed.

behavior: Conan recognizes `tools.cmake:configure_args` as a supported configuration entry for CMake integration.
When `CMake.configure()` constructs the configure command, it appends each argument from `tools.cmake:configure_args` to that command line.
The extra configure arguments are injected after the CMakeLists/source folder argument used for the configure call.
Automatic CMake log-level arguments continue to be added afterward when they are not already supplied through explicit CLI arguments.
When `tools.cmake:configure_args` is absent, no additional configure arguments are added.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer sets `tools.cmake:configure_args` to multiple arguments and invokes `CMake.configure()`, the resulting CMake configure command should include those arguments as separate command-line entries.
When `tools.cmake:configure_args` includes values such as extra `-D` definitions or flags like `--fresh`, `CMake.configure()` should forward them to the configure invocation.
When `tools.cmake:configure_args` is not configured, `CMake.configure()` should produce the same configure command behavior as before the upgrade.
When automatic log-level handling is active, arguments from `tools.cmake:configure_args` should appear before automatically injected log-level options.
Setting `tools.cmake:configure_args` should not alter the behavior of non-configure CMake operations.

task_13.title: Fix CMakeConfigDeps build-context property overrides
task_13.description: Conan 2.27.0 fixes CMakeConfigDeps so properties customized with set_property() are resolved correctly for build requirements. This makes generated CMake package names and related metadata honor build-context overrides instead of falling back to the default dependency definition.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps applies set_property() overrides correctly for dependencies consumed in the build context, so custom CMake package metadata for build requirements is honored during generation.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeConfigDeps retrieves a property for a dependency, it must resolve that property according to the declared requirement context, including build requirements. Overrides registered through CMakeConfigDeps.set_property() for a build-context dependency must be returned by property lookup and reflected in generated CMake metadata such as overridden package naming via properties like cmake_file_name.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to customize CMakeConfigDeps output for tool or build dependencies the same way they can for regular dependencies. If they rename or override a build requirement's CMake-facing metadata, the generated CMake files should consistently use that customized value.

constraints.grounded: Property resolution must remain context-aware so build-context overrides stay isolated from host-context overrides for the same dependency name. Existing behavior for non-build dependencies, component scoping, and normal property retrieval must continue to work without regression.
constraints.conceptual: Customizations should apply only to the dependency instance and context they were defined for. The fix must not change how unrelated dependencies or existing host-side configurations behave.

behavior: CMakeConfigDeps now determines property lookup context from the declared requirement so build requirements are recognized correctly during generation.
Properties assigned with set_property() for a build-context dependency are now honored instead of being missed because of incorrect context resolution.
Observable CMake outputs derived from those properties, including customized package/file naming used for dependency discovery, now reflect the build-context override.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer sets a CMakeConfigDeps property such as cmake_file_name for a build requirement, the generated CMake integration should use the overridden name for that dependency.
When the same package name can exist in different dependency contexts, a build-context property override should apply only to the build requirement and should not leak into the host requirement.
When generating CMakeConfigDeps files for ordinary non-build dependencies, property lookup and generated metadata should continue to behave as before.

task_12.title: Preserve hexadecimal NMake defines as numeric macros
task_12.description: The upgrade fixes Conan's NMake integrations so assigned preprocessor defines with hexadecimal numeric values, such as Windows version macros, are generated as numeric compiler definitions instead of quoted string values. It also aligns define formatting between toolchain-generated and dependency-generated NMake compiler flags.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that NMake integrations treat hexadecimal assigned defines such as `WINVER=0x0601` as numeric macros rather than string-valued macros, and ensure the same define-formatting behavior is applied whether the define comes from project toolchain settings or dependency metadata.

expectation.grounded: When `NMakeToolchain` formats project defines and when `NMakeDeps` formats dependency `cpp_info.defines`, assigned defines must continue to be emitted as `CL` `/D` definitions compatible with NMake, but values that are numeric, including hexadecimal values such as `0x0601`, must remain unquoted. Assigned values that are not numeric must continue to be emitted with quoting, and defines without a value or with an empty value must remain supported.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, NMake-based builds should preserve hexadecimal macro values as numbers so code that relies on numeric preprocessor comparisons continues to work correctly. Textual macro values should still behave as text, and users should see the same behavior regardless of whether a define is declared locally or supplied by a dependency.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing NMake define handling for bare defines, empty assignments, decimal numeric assignments, or non-numeric assignments containing spaces or symbols. The observable define formatting rules must remain consistent across both `NMakeToolchain` and `NMakeDeps` outputs.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to incorrect hexadecimal-value handling and should not change unrelated define semantics. Existing valid numeric and textual macro definitions should continue to work the same way across all NMake-generated compiler flags.

behavior: Hexadecimal assigned define values such as `WINVER=0x0601` are emitted for NMake compiler flags as numeric macro values instead of quoted string values.
Decimal assigned define values continue to be emitted without added quoting.
Assigned define values that are not numeric continue to be emitted with quoting so textual values remain preserved in generated compiler flags.
The same define-formatting rules are now applied to defines generated by `NMakeToolchain` and defines propagated through `NMakeDeps`.
Defines without an assigned value and defines with an empty assigned value continue to be accepted in generated NMake compiler flags.
acceptance_criteria: When a project configured with `NMakeToolchain` declares a define like `WINVER=0x0601`, the generated NMake compiler flags should preserve `0x0601` as a numeric macro value rather than a quoted string.
When a dependency exposes `cpp_info.defines` containing a hexadecimal numeric assignment, `NMakeDeps` should generate compiler flags that preserve that value as numeric.
When a define uses a decimal numeric assignment such as `FOO=7`, generated NMake compiler flags should continue to treat the value as numeric and not quote it.
When a define uses a non-numeric assigned value, including values with spaces or symbolic expressions, generated NMake compiler flags should continue to quote that value appropriately.
When equivalent defines are supplied from project configuration and dependency metadata, the generated NMake compiler flags should apply the same formatting behavior in both cases.

task_15.title: Separate build and host package grouping in HTML graph output
task_15.description: The HTML output of `conan graph info` now avoids merging packages that share the same displayed label across build and host contexts. This preserves distinct nodes and dependency links for each context so the rendered graph reflects the actual package relationships.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan graph info .. -f=html` groups repeated packages only within the same dependency context, so packages that appear in both build and host graphs remain separately visible and keep their correct dependency relationships.

expectation.grounded: In the HTML formatter for `conan graph info`, package collapsing must treat `build` and `host` nodes as separate grouping domains. When `collapse_packages` is active, a node may collapse only into an existing node with the same rendered package label and the same `context`. Packages with the same label in different contexts must render as distinct nodes with their own edges.
expectation.conceptual: The HTML dependency graph should no longer merge build-time and host-time packages just because they have the same package label. Users should be able to see separate package instances per context, with each one connected to the dependencies that actually belong to it.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing ability to collapse repeated packages within a single context. Existing graph visibility controls such as hiding build or test nodes must continue to apply, and the fix must avoid introducing phantom root packages or misattached dependency edges caused by cross-context collapsing.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the graph compact where duplicates are truly equivalent, but do not sacrifice correctness by combining nodes that represent different dependency roles. Existing filtering behavior should remain intact.

behavior: When the HTML graph contains the same package label in both `build` and `host` contexts, the rendered output shows separate collapsed nodes for each context instead of one merged node.
When repeated package nodes share both the same label and the same context, they can still be grouped into a single collapsed node in the HTML graph.
Dependency edges are preserved per context, so each rendered package node keeps only the requirements that belong to that build or host package instance.
The HTML graph no longer misrepresents mixed build/host dependency trees by dropping one package instance or inventing an unrelated root package as a side effect of collapsing.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan graph info .. -f=html` renders a graph where the same package appears once as a build requirement and once as a host requirement, it should show both package instances separately in the HTML graph.
When those build and host package instances depend on different downstream packages, the HTML graph should keep the corresponding dependency links attached to the correct package instance.
When multiple nodes with the same package label appear within the same dependency context, the HTML graph may still collapse them into one node rather than expanding every duplicate.
When build requirements are hidden, build-context nodes should remain omitted as before, without affecting the correctness of the remaining host graph.

task_14.title: Validate exact versions in platform requirement profiles
task_14.description: Conan 2.27.0 improves profile validation for platform replacement requirements. Profiles that declare `[platform_requires]` or `[platform_tool_requires]` with version ranges are now rejected immediately with a clear user-facing error, making it explicit that these sections only accept exact recipe versions. Deprecated `[system_tools]` profile usage remains supported as a legacy alias for platform tool requirements and continues to warn.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan profiles reject `[platform_requires]` and `[platform_tool_requires]` entries that use version ranges, and report a clear user-facing error that these sections only accept exact versions.

expectation.grounded: When Conan loads profile sections `[platform_requires]` or `[platform_tool_requires]`, each entry should be parsed as a `RecipeReference` and validated to use an exact version. If any entry resolves to a version range instead of a concrete version, profile loading should fail with a `ConanException` that clearly identifies these sections as requiring exact versions. Deprecated `[system_tools]` input should still be accepted as the source for platform tool requirements and should continue to emit a deprecation warning.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading to Conan 2.27.0 should get an immediate, clear configuration error if they place version ranges in platform replacement requirement sections. These profile sections are for pinned platform recipes only, while the deprecated legacy alias should still behave compatibly apart from warning the user.

constraints.grounded: The validation must apply specifically to `[platform_requires]` and `[platform_tool_requires]`, including values supplied through the deprecated `[system_tools]` alias. Exact-version entries that were previously valid should continue to load normally. The error should be raised during profile reading rather than surfacing later as an unrelated low-level failure.
constraints.conceptual: Only invalid platform replacement declarations should be blocked. Valid pinned platform requirements should keep working, and existing legacy profile usage should not silently change behavior beyond producing a deprecation warning and clearer validation errors.

behavior: Profiles now validate platform replacement entries before continuing with dependency processing.
Any `[platform_requires]` entry using a version range is rejected as an invalid profile definition.
Any `[platform_tool_requires]` entry using a version range is rejected as an invalid profile definition.
When the deprecated `[system_tools]` section is used, its contents are treated as platform tool requirements and still produce a deprecation warning.
Invalid version-range usage in these sections now results in a clear `ConanException` instead of an opaque assertion-style failure.
acceptance_criteria: When a profile defines `[platform_requires]` with only exact recipe versions, Conan should load the profile successfully.
When a profile defines `[platform_tool_requires]` with only exact recipe versions, Conan should load the profile successfully.
When a profile defines `[platform_requires]` with a version range, Conan should stop while reading the profile and report that exact versions are required for platform replacement sections.
When a profile defines `[platform_tool_requires]` with a version range, Conan should stop while reading the profile and report that exact versions are required for platform replacement sections.
When a profile uses the deprecated `[system_tools]` section, Conan should continue to interpret it as platform tool requirements and emit a deprecation warning.

task_16.title: Make lockfile overrides context-aware
task_16.description: The upgrade fixes lockfile override handling so that overrides recorded in a lockfile are only applied to dependency resolution in the matching context. This prevents host overrides from altering build requirements, and build overrides from altering host requirements, while preserving valid override behavior inside the correct locked context.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that lockfile-based overrides are applied only within the dependency context they were locked for, so installs and graph resolution do not fail or silently rewrite dependencies when host and build requirements coexist.

expectation.grounded: When Conan applies overrides from a lockfile during dependency graph resolution, it should resolve an override for a requirement only if the override target is present in the locked references for the current context. Requirements resolved in the host context should only consume overrides from host locked requirements, and requirements resolved in the build context should only consume overrides from build locked requirements. Valid overrides in the matching context should continue to update the requirement to the overridden reference and preserve override tracking metadata.
expectation.conceptual: Lockfile overrides should behave predictably in mixed host/build dependency graphs. An override captured for one side of the graph must not leak into the other side, and upgrades should continue to honor overrides that belong to the current dependency context.

constraints.grounded: Do not apply a lockfile override when the overridden reference is not locked in the current resolution context. Do not regress existing behavior for overrides whose target reference is locked in the same context. The change must affect runtime graph resolution behavior rather than requiring manual lockfile edits.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to preventing cross-context override leakage. Legitimate overrides must still work, and unrelated lockfile behavior should remain unchanged.

behavior: Lockfile override resolution now considers whether the current requirement is being resolved in the host or build context.
An override stored in the lockfile is ignored for a requirement if its target reference is not part of the locked references for the current context.
Host-context overrides no longer rewrite build requirements solely because the same package reference appears in both contexts.
Build-context overrides no longer rewrite host requirements solely because the same package reference appears in both contexts.
Overrides that belong to the active context continue to update the resolved requirement to the locked override reference.
acceptance_criteria: When resolving a dependency graph with a lockfile that contains a host-side override, build requirements should remain unchanged unless the override target is also locked for the build context.
When resolving a dependency graph with a lockfile that contains a build-side override, host requirements should remain unchanged unless the override target is also locked for the host context.
When a lockfile contains an override whose target reference is locked in the same context as the current requirement, Conan should still resolve that requirement to the overridden reference.
When a package reference appears in both host and build graphs, applying a lockfile should not cause cross-context override errors or incorrect dependency substitutions.

task_18.title: Complete legacy CMakeConfigDeps library variables for component packages
task_18.description: The upgrade fixes `CMakeConfigDeps` so the legacy `<packagename>_LIBRARIES` variable includes all generated library targets for packages that expose multiple components. This restores backward compatibility for consumers that still read the legacy variable instead of linking only through newer imported targets.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `CMakeConfigDeps` generates a complete legacy `<packagename>_LIBRARIES` variable for componentized packages so consumers using legacy CMake variables receive every relevant library target instead of an incomplete list.

expectation.grounded: When `CMakeConfigDeps` generates config files for a package, the legacy `<packagename>_LIBRARIES` variable must include every exported component target when the package has components. For each component entry, it should use that component's `cmake_target_name` property when defined, otherwise the default `<packagename>::<component>` target name. Packages without components must continue to expose the single package target in the legacy variable.
expectation.conceptual: Legacy CMake consumers should see a complete list of linkable targets in `<packagename>_LIBRARIES`. Multi-component packages should expose all component targets there, while single-target packages should keep the existing single entry behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public role of `CMakeConfigDeps` legacy variables beyond correcting omitted libraries. Preserve support for packages with no components, preserve component-specific target renaming through `cmake_target_name`, and keep the legacy variable consumable as a space-separated list of targets.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be backward compatible. It should add missing library targets for legacy consumers without changing how non-component packages are represented or breaking custom target naming.

behavior: For packages with components, the generated legacy `<packagename>_LIBRARIES` variable now contains all exported component targets instead of only a single root target.
If a component defines a custom `cmake_target_name`, that custom target name is what appears in the legacy `<packagename>_LIBRARIES` variable for that component.
If a component does not define a custom target name, the legacy variable uses the default `<packagename>::<component>` target name for that component.
Packages without components continue to populate `<packagename>_LIBRARIES` with the package-level target as before.
Legacy CMake code that links or inspects `<packagename>_LIBRARIES` can now discover all component libraries from generated `CMakeConfigDeps` files.
acceptance_criteria: When a package exposes multiple components and `CMakeConfigDeps` generates its config files, `<packagename>_LIBRARIES` should list every component target that consumers are expected to link.
When a componentized package uses custom `cmake_target_name` values, `<packagename>_LIBRARIES` should expose those custom target names rather than only default names.
When a package has no components, `<packagename>_LIBRARIES` should still resolve to the single package target.
When legacy CMake consumer code reads `<packagename>_LIBRARIES`, it should no longer miss component libraries that are part of the package's exported interface.

task_17.title: Clarify source backup authentication failures
task_17.description: Upgrading from 2.26.2 to 2.27.0 improves user-facing error reporting when Conan cannot access a source backup server because authentication or permissions are rejected. Backup source download and upload still fail, but the failure is now explicitly described as an authentication failure and directs users to verify their source credentials configuration.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that authentication failures against source backup servers during backup source download or upload are reported as clear credential failures and direct users to verify their source credentials configuration.

expectation.grounded: When Conan encounters an AuthenticationException or ForbiddenException while accessing a source backup server for backup source download or upload, it should raise ConanException that identifies the source backup server, indicates that authentication failed, and tells the user to check 'source_credentials.json'.
expectation.conceptual: If a configured source backup server rejects access during source retrieval or source backup upload, users should see a clear error explaining that authentication to that server failed and that their source credentials configuration should be reviewed.

constraints.grounded: Auth-related failures on source backup server access must continue surfacing as ConanException for both download and upload paths, include the relevant backup server identity and underlying auth/forbidden cause, and must not alter existing non-auth handling such as missing backup files.
constraints.conceptual: Only the clarity of credential-related failure reporting should change. Successful source backup operations and unrelated source backup error handling should continue to behave as before.

behavior: Source backup download now reports backup-server authentication rejection as a ConanException framed as an authentication failure and advises checking 'source_credentials.json'.
Source backup upload now reports backup-server authentication or permission rejection as a ConanException framed as an authentication failure and advises checking 'source_credentials.json'.
The reported failure continues to expose which source backup server failed and preserves the underlying authentication-related error context.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan tries to download backup sources from a configured source backup server and that server rejects authentication or authorization, it should fail with ConanException that states authentication to the source backup server failed and tells the user to check 'source_credentials.json'.

When Conan tries to upload backup sources to a configured source backup server and that server rejects authentication or authorization, it should fail with ConanException that states authentication to the source backup server failed and tells the user to check 'source_credentials.json'.

When a backup source is unavailable on the source backup server for reasons unrelated to authentication, Conan should continue using the existing non-auth failure or warning behavior rather than reporting a credential failure.
When valid source backup credentials are configured, source backup download and upload should continue completing with their existing success behavior.

task_19.title: Relax implicit language validation in CMakeConfigDeps
task_19.description: Conan 2.27.0 updates CMakeConfigDeps so generated CMake package configuration files stop rejecting valid consumer projects that rely on CMake's implicit language compatibility. Consumers should be able to link C dependencies from CXX-only projects, and equivalent implicit compatibility should be honored for CUDA, while real unsupported language mismatches still fail during configuration.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps-generated package configuration files do not fail valid CMake consumer projects when dependency link languages are already implicitly supported by the consumer project's enabled languages.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeConfigDeps validates dependency `link_languages` against CMake `ENABLED_LANGUAGES`, it should treat `CXX` as satisfying `C`, and `CUDA` as satisfying both `C` and `CXX`, before deciding whether to raise a configuration error for a missing language. A consumer using `find_package(... CONFIG)` from CMakeConfigDeps should therefore be able to link a dependency with C linkage from a `project()` that enables only `CXX` without explicitly declaring `C`.
expectation.conceptual: Generated CMake dependency configs should follow CMake's own implicit language rules. Valid consumer projects must configure successfully without redundant language declarations, while truly incompatible language requirements should still be blocked.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the existing validation that checks dependency `link_languages` against the consumer project's enabled languages, and only relax it for the implicit relationships shown by the update: `CXX` implies `C`, and `CUDA` implies `C` and `CXX`. Do not remove the configuration-time error path for unsupported link languages outside those relationships.
constraints.conceptual: Keep protection against invalid language mismatches, but eliminate false failures caused by requiring users to restate language support that CMake already provides implicitly.

behavior: A consumer project that enables only `CXX` is treated as compatible with dependencies whose generated CMake config declares C linkage.
A consumer project that enables `CUDA` is treated as compatible with dependencies that declare C linkage.
A consumer project that enables `CUDA` is treated as compatible with dependencies that declare C++ linkage.

Generated CMake configs still surface a configuration error when a dependency requires a link language that is neither explicitly enabled nor implicitly satisfied by these CMake language relationships.
acceptance_criteria: When a package consumed through CMakeConfigDeps declares C linkage and the consumer CMake project is declared with `project(... CXX)`, configuration should succeed without requiring `C` to be added explicitly.
When a package consumed through CMakeConfigDeps declares C linkage and the consumer project enables `CUDA`, configuration should not fail language validation for that dependency.
When a package consumed through CMakeConfigDeps declares C++ linkage and the consumer project enables `CUDA`, configuration should not fail language validation for that dependency.

When a dependency requires a link language that the consumer project neither enables nor implicitly satisfies through these rules, the generated config should still fail configuration rather than accepting the mismatch.

task_21.title: Handle editable builds safely when source download is forced
task_21.description: This update fixes a crash path in Conan when users run operations with `--build=editable` while also enabling `tools.build:download_source=True`. Editable dependencies, including editable packages selected for build, should no longer go through source-download handling that assumes cached recipe layouts, avoiding assertions and allowing the command to complete normally.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan operations using `--build=editable` remain stable when `tools.build:download_source=True` is enabled, and that editable dependencies do not trigger source-download processing or crash during the install/build flow.

expectation.grounded: When Conan evaluates dependencies during install/build flows with `tools.build:download_source=True`, packages marked as editable must be excluded from source-download handling not only for `BINARY_EDITABLE` but also for `BINARY_EDITABLE_BUILD`. Using `--build=editable` with editable requirements must therefore complete without an assertion caused by recipe layout access for editable nodes.
expectation.conceptual: Conan should recognize all editable dependency states as non-cache-backed editables when forced source download is enabled. Users who opt into `--build=editable` should see normal command execution instead of a crash, and editable packages should not run source acquisition as part of that flow.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve the existing behavior that editable dependencies are skipped by source-download processing when `tools.build:download_source=True` is set. Non-editable packages must continue to follow normal source-download behavior, and the change must not require users to disable either `--build=editable` or the configuration flag to avoid failure.
constraints.conceptual: The update should only remove the invalid handling of editable packages under forced source download, without changing how regular packages download sources or how editable mode otherwise behaves.

behavior: Operations that combine `--build=editable` with `tools.build:download_source=True` no longer fail due to an internal assertion on editable dependencies.
Editable dependencies selected for build are treated as editable for source-download decisions and are skipped instead of being processed like cached binaries.
Forced source download continues to apply to eligible non-editable dependencies only.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs a Conan operation with `--build=editable` and `tools.build:download_source=True`, it should complete without raising an assertion caused by an editable dependency.
When a dependency is in an editable state, enabling forced source download should not attempt source-download handling for that dependency, even if it is selected by `--build=editable`.
When a dependency is not editable, enabling `tools.build:download_source=True` should continue to preserve normal source-download behavior.

task_20.title: Fix Conan user preset stubs for custom user_presets_path
task_20.description: Conan 2.27.0 fixes CMake preset generation when a project uses a custom user presets file through `user_presets_path`. The generated user preset file now derives stub presets from the actual included preset files, avoids redundant stubs when a real preset already exists, and emits valid build and test stubs so user-defined preset inheritance remains usable across regenerated or partially available Conan preset sets.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when `CMakeToolchain.user_presets_path` is specified, Conan generates valid user CMake preset stubs for inherited Conan presets so user-defined configure, build, and test presets continue to work even if some inherited Conan presets are not currently present as real presets in the included Conan preset files.

expectation.grounded: When Conan generates the user presets file for `CMakeToolchain.user_presets_path`, it should inspect the preset files referenced through `include` and create stub entries only for inherited preset names that are missing from the included `configurePresets`, `buildPresets`, or `testPresets`. Generated `buildPresets` and `testPresets` stubs must include the corresponding `configurePreset` linkage so they remain valid CMake presets. If an included preset file already defines a real preset of the same type and name, Conan should not emit a duplicate stub for that preset type.
expectation.conceptual: Using a custom Conan-generated user presets file should produce a complete and valid preset graph for any user preset that inherits Conan presets. Missing inherited presets should be represented by safe placeholder entries, while real presets from included files should be used directly without duplication.

constraints.grounded: Conan should only add stub presets for inherited names requested by the user preset file, should not replace real presets already available through included preset files, and should preserve valid inclusion of the Conan preset file regardless of whether the include path is stored as relative or absolute. Existing user preset files that are not marked as Conan-managed must remain untouched.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to keeping custom user preset generation valid and non-destructive. It must not introduce duplicate preset definitions, break existing includes, or overwrite user-owned preset files that Conan does not manage.

behavior: Conan now computes user preset stubs after the user preset file has been linked to its included Conan preset files, so stub generation reflects the actual presets available through those includes.

For each inherited configure, build, and test preset name, Conan emits a stub in the generated user presets file only when no included preset file already provides a real preset of the same type and name.
Generated build preset stubs include a `configurePreset` reference to the same preset name, making the stub a valid CMake build preset.
Generated test preset stubs include a `configurePreset` reference to the same preset name, making the stub a valid CMake test preset.

If the currently included Conan preset files only contain a subset of the inherited preset names, Conan still preserves the missing inherited names as stubs in the user presets file instead of dropping them.
acceptance_criteria: When a project sets `CMakeToolchain.user_presets_path` and a user preset inherits a Conan preset name that is not defined in the currently included preset files, Conan should generate a stub preset of the appropriate type in the user presets file.

When an included Conan preset file already defines a configure, build, or test preset with the inherited name, Conan should not generate a second stub of that same preset type and name in the user presets file.
When Conan generates a build or test stub for an inherited preset name, the resulting preset should include the required configure preset association so CMake can treat it as valid.

When the set of generated Conan presets changes between runs and some inherited preset names are temporarily absent from the included preset files, the user presets file should still contain stubs for those inherited names so user preset inheritance remains valid.

task_22.title: Fix Emscripten compiler auto-detection on first run and Windows
task_22.description: The upgrade fixes Conan's Emscripten compiler detection so automatic identification no longer fails when `emcc --version` emits additional output before the version banner, a situation that can occur on first run and on Windows. Detection now evaluates the full command output and only succeeds when Emscripten and a parseable semantic version are present.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Emscripten compiler auto-detection succeeds on first run and on Windows even when `emcc --version` prints extra lines before the version banner, while still rejecting outputs that are not valid Emscripten version reports.

expectation.grounded: When `detect_emcc_compiler` runs `emcc --version`, it should treat the full command output as the detection source, not only the first output line. The function should return `("emcc", Version(<detected version>), compiler_exe)` when the output contains an Emscripten signature and a semantic version anywhere in the output. It should return `(None, None, None)` when the command exits with a non-zero status, when the output does not identify Emscripten, or when no semantic version can be parsed.
expectation.conceptual: Automatic Emscripten detection should work reliably across platforms and fresh environments, including cases where the compiler prints setup or sanity-check information before its actual version line. Detection should only succeed for genuine Emscripten output with a valid version and otherwise behave as a clean no-match.

constraints.grounded: Do not require the Emscripten banner or version to appear on the first line of `emcc --version` output. Do not report an `emcc` compiler match if the command fails, if the output lacks an Emscripten identifier, or if no semantic version in `major.minor.patch` form is present.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must broaden compatibility with real `emcc` output formats without making compiler detection looser for unrelated or malformed outputs. Failed detection should remain non-destructive and should not create a false positive compiler identification.

behavior: `detect_emcc_compiler` now scans the entire `emcc --version` output for an Emscripten identifier instead of depending on the first output line.
Version extraction for `detect_emcc_compiler` now searches the full command output and succeeds when a semantic version appears anywhere in that output.
If `emcc --version` exits with a non-zero status, `detect_emcc_compiler` continues to return no detected compiler.
If the output does not contain an Emscripten identifier or does not contain a parseable semantic version, `detect_emcc_compiler` returns no detected compiler.
acceptance_criteria: When `emcc --version` prints one or more informational lines before the normal Emscripten version banner, automatic compiler detection should still identify `emcc` and expose the detected semantic version.
When `emcc --version` output includes the Emscripten banner and a semantic version anywhere in the output, detection should return the `emcc` compiler identity with that version.
When the version command exits unsuccessfully, detection should report no compiler match.
When the output does not correspond to Emscripten or does not include a parseable semantic version, detection should report no compiler match.

task_23.title: Honor run-scope Windows bash settings in ConanFile.run
task_23.description: Conan 2.27.0 fixes Windows bash execution for recipe commands run with `scope="run"`. When a recipe enables `win_bash_run=True`, `ConanFile.run()` should apply the run-scope bash environment instead of defaulting to build-scope bash behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Windows recipes using `win_bash_run=True` can execute `self.run(..., scope="run")` through the configured bash environment with the correct run-scope behavior.

expectation.grounded: `ConanFile.run()` must honor its `scope` argument when wrapping command execution. On Windows, `self.run(..., scope="run")` with `win_bash_run=True` should use run-scope bash handling, rather than relying on build-scope `win_bash` behavior.
expectation.conceptual: When a recipe opts into Windows bash for run-time commands, run-scoped shell invocations should execute in that bash environment as configured, without silently behaving like build-scoped commands.

constraints.grounded: Existing build-scope behavior for `self.run(..., scope="build")` with `win_bash=True` must remain intact. Run-scope bash support must work independently of whether build-scope bash is enabled.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should preserve current build-time bash behavior while making run-time bash opt-in work independently and predictably.

behavior: `ConanFile.run()` uses the provided `scope` to determine how command execution is wrapped.
On Windows, `self.run(..., scope="run")` respects `win_bash_run=True` instead of behaving as a build-scoped bash invocation.
Run-scoped commands executed through the configured Windows bash integration receive the expected bash-based execution environment for the run scope.
acceptance_criteria: When a Windows recipe enables `win_bash_run=True` and invokes `self.run(..., scope="run")`, the command should execute through the configured bash environment for the run scope.
When a Windows recipe uses `self.run(..., scope="build")` with `win_bash=True`, build-scope bash execution should continue to behave as before.
When `win_bash_run=True` is enabled but `win_bash=True` is not, a `scope="run"` invocation should still receive run-scope bash handling.

task_24.title: Fix custom make program paths in Windows subsystem Autotools builds
task_24.description: The upgrade fixes Conan Autotools builds on Windows subsystem environments so a configured `tools.gnu:make_program` is translated into the subsystem-compatible path format before execution. This prevents build failures when users provide a Windows-native path for the make executable while running through environments such as MSYS2.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan Autotools builds running inside a Windows subsystem correctly honor `tools.gnu:make_program` when the make executable is configured using a native Windows path, so users can override the make binary without path-format-related build failures.

expectation.grounded: When `Autotools.make()` resolves the make executable from `tools.gnu:make_program` in a Windows subsystem build context, it should normalize that configured program through the active subsystem path translation before launching the command. The configured make executable should remain the one that is executed, but its path must be accepted by the subsystem shell environment.
expectation.conceptual: If a user selects a custom make executable for an Autotools build running under a Windows Unix-like subsystem, Conan should run that tool successfully even when the configured path is written in normal Windows form.

constraints.grounded: The fix should preserve existing `Autotools.make()` argument handling, job configuration, and default make selection behavior, and only adjust how the chosen make program is represented for the detected build subsystem. Non-subsystem and already compatible invocations must continue to work without behavioral regression.
constraints.conceptual: The change should only make custom make-path handling more robust in subsystem-based Windows builds and should not alter unrelated build semantics or break existing configurations that already work.

behavior: A `tools.gnu:make_program` value is now interpreted in the active Windows build subsystem context before `Autotools.make()` invokes it.
Windows-native paths configured for the make executable are accepted in subsystem-backed Autotools builds instead of failing because the shell cannot resolve the path format.
The subsystem used for path conversion is determined from the build-side environment, so the executed make command matches the active bash-like subsystem.
Default make-program resolution and the rest of the make command construction remain unchanged apart from subsystem path normalization of the selected executable.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan Autotools build runs in a Windows subsystem environment and `tools.gnu:make_program` points to a make executable using a Windows-native path, the build should invoke that executable successfully through `Autotools.make()`.
When a custom make executable is configured for a subsystem-backed Autotools build, Conan should honor the configured tool rather than falling back to a different make command.
When `Autotools.make()` runs outside the affected Windows subsystem path-translation scenario, its existing make-program selection and invocation behavior should remain unchanged.
